Y'shua.note: The Hebrew writing of this name in the later books. The older form is יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, Yehoshua. Matthew ties the name to salvation, not to a pronunciation of the Syriac.
The Greek New Testament writes the name this way. It is a Greek spelling of the Hebrew, not a different person.

Keefa.note: The name is Aramaic, a rock. These are Hebrew letters writing that Aramaic word. The Greek Πέτρος is the translation, kept in this book as Petros.

Petros.note: The Greek name, meaning a rock. In this Peshitta the man’s own name is Keefa. Petros is the Greek form where the text uses it.

Maryam.note: The Hebrew writing of Miriam. The Greek scriptures use Μαρία and Μαριάμ.

Moshe.note: The Hebrew writing. The Greek is Μωϋσῆς.

Dawid.note: The Hebrew writing. The Greek is Δαυίδ.

Avraham.note: The Hebrew writing. The older form of the name is אַבְרָם, Avram. The Greek is Ἀβραάμ.

Ya'akov.note: One Hebrew name. This Peshitta uses it for the patriarch and for James. The Greek is Ἰάκωβος.

Yosip.note: The Hebrew writing. The Greek is Ἰωσήφ.

Yochanan.note: The Hebrew writing, “YHWH is gracious.” The Greek is Ἰωάννης.

Shimon.note: The Hebrew writing. A few verses in this Peshitta use the Greek-shaped spelling ܣܝܡܘܢ instead.

Shaul.note: The Hebrew writing. The Greek form of this man’s Hebrew name is Σαῦλος. Paulos is the other name.

Paulos.note: A Greek name from the Latin Paulus. It is not a Hebrew name. The Hebrew name of this man is Shaul.

Andrawos.note: A Greek name. The Syriac writes the Greek, it does not translate it.

Toma.note: Aramaic for twin. The Greek Θωμᾶς is the same word written in Greek letters.

Bar-Tulmay.note: Aramaic bar, “son of,” with the name Talmai. The Greek writes the whole name as one word.

Matai.note: A short Hebrew form of Mattityahu. The Greek is Μαθθαῖος.

Bar-Naba.note: Aramaic bar with a second word. The book itself says the name is read as “son of consolation.”

Timotheos.note: A Greek name, “one who honors God.”

Titus.note: A Greek name from the Latin Titus.

Luqa.note: A Greek name from the Latin Lucas.

Marqos.note: A Greek name from the Latin Marcus.

Pilatos.note: A Latin name. The Greek writes Πιλᾶτος. There is no Hebrew form of this name.

Herodes.note: A Greek name. The men called Herodes in this book are not one person.

Caesar.note: A Latin title and name. The Greek is Καῖσαρ. The Syriac Qesar is that word, not a Hebrew name.

Urishlim.note: The Hebrew writing of Jerusalem. The Greek uses Ἱεροσόλυμα and Ἰερουσαλήμ.

Galila.note: The Hebrew writing. The Greek is Γαλιλαία.

Yehud.note: The Hebrew name of the land of Judah. The Greek for the land is Ἰουδαία.

Yehuda.note: One Hebrew name. This book uses it for the patriarch Judah, for Judas, and for Jude.

Natsrath.note: The Hebrew writing of Nazareth. The Greek is Ναζαρέτ.

Yordanan.note: The Hebrew writing of the Jordan. The Greek is Ἰορδάνης.

Mitsrayin.note: The Hebrew writing of Egypt. The Greek is Αἴγυπτος.

Bavel.note: The Hebrew writing of Babylon. The Greek is Βαβυλών.

Darmasuq.note: The Hebrew writing of Damascus. The Greek is Δαμασκός.

Tsidon.note: The Hebrew writing of Sidon. The Greek is Σιδών.

Tsur.note: The Hebrew writing of Tyre. The Greek is Τύρος.

Tsehyon.note: The Hebrew writing of Zion. The Greek is Σιών.

Sinai.note: The Hebrew writing. The Greek is Σινᾶ.

Sdom.note: The Hebrew writing of Sodom. The Greek is Σόδομα.

Beth-Lekhem.note: Hebrew for “house of bread.” The Greek is Βηθλέεμ.

Kfar-Nachum.note: Hebrew for “village of Nachum.” The Greek is Καφαρναούμ.

Qesarya.note: A Greek place-name formed from Caesar. The Syriac follows the Greek.

Rhoma.note: The Greek writing of Rome. The Latin is Roma.

Athens.note: The Greek name of the city. The Syriac writes that name.

Ephesos.note: The Greek name of the city.

Antiokia.note: The Greek name. This book also prints Antiokia for the same Syriac.

Tesaloniqa.note: The Greek name of the city.

Surya.note: The Greek name of the land. This book also prints Syria.

Noach.note: The Hebrew writing. One genealogy verse in this book prints Nuch for the same Syriac. The Greek is Νῶε.

Nuch.note: The Hebrew writing of Noah. The Greek is Νῶε.

Adam.note: The Hebrew writing. The Greek is Ἀδάμ.

Habel.note: The Hebrew writing of Abel. This book also prints Habeel.

Yitz'chak.note: The Hebrew writing of Isaac. The Greek is Ἰσαάκ.

Sara.note: The Hebrew writing. The older form is שָׂרַי, Sarai.

Eliyahu.note: The Hebrew writing of Elijah. The Greek is Ἠλίας.

Eshaya.note: The Hebrew writing of Isaiah. The Greek is Ἠσαΐας.

Shlemun.note: The Hebrew writing of Solomon. The Greek is Σολομών.

Aharon.note: The Hebrew writing of Aaron. The Greek is Ἀαρών.

Levi.note: The Hebrew writing of the patriarch and of the priestly tribe.

Elishaba.note: The Hebrew writing. The Greek form of this name is Ἐλισάβετ.

Lazar.note: The Hebrew name behind Lazar. The Greek short form is Λάζαρος.

Martha.note: An Aramaic name, “lady.” The Greek is Μάρθα.

Magdalitha.note: A woman from Magdala. The Greek is an adjective of that place, not a second personal name.

Satana.note: The Hebrew word for an adversary. The Greek is Σατανᾶς. The lexicon note on this stem is the study of the word in this book.

Sheol.note: The Hebrew name of the place of the dead. The Greek often writes ᾅδης for the same place.

Gehenna.note: Hebrew for the valley of Hinnom. The Greek is Γέεννα. The Syriac writes that name as one word.

Gabri'el.note: The Hebrew writing. The Greek is Γαβριήλ.

Gabriel.note: The Hebrew writing. The Greek is Γαβριήλ.

Mikael.note: The Hebrew writing. The Greek is Μιχαήλ.

Abba.note: Aramaic for father, written here in Hebrew letters. It is the word itself, not a Greek translation. The Greek keeps Ἀββᾶ.

Yisrael.note: The Hebrew writing of the man and of the people. The Greek is Ἰσραήλ.

Ammanu'el.note: Hebrew for “God is with us.” The verse itself gives that reading.

Malkizedeq.note: Hebrew for “my king is righteousness.” The Greek is Μελχισέδεκ.

Achaia.note: The Greek name of the Roman province. The Syriac writes that name.

Asia.note: The Greek name of the Roman province. The same Syriac letters are also the ordinary word for a physician.

Felix.note: A Latin name. The Greek is Φῆλιξ. This book also prints Pilkas for the same Syriac.

Pilkas.note: The Latin name. The Greek is Φῆλιξ.

ܝܗܘܕܝܐ.note: A person of Judah. The Greek New Testament writes Ἰουδαῖος.

ܢܨܪܝܐ.note: A person of Nazareth. The Syriac town-name is Natsrath.

ܝܘܢܐ.note: The Hebrew name, and the ordinary word for a dove. The Greek writes Ἰωνᾶς.

ܚܢܢ.note: Gracious. The Greek writes the high priest Ἅννας, Annas.

ܡܠܟܝܙܕܩ.note: My king is righteousness. The Greek writes Μελχισέδεκ.

ܐܣܛܦܢܐ.note: A Greek name, from stephanos, a wreath.

ܒܪܢܝܩܐ.note: A Macedonian Greek name, bearer of victory.

ܣܘܣܬܢܣ.note: A Greek name. The Syriac writes those sounds.

ܐܠܟܣܢܕܪܣ.note: Defender of men. A Greek name.

ܕܡܝܛܪܝܘܣ.note: Belonging to Demeter. A Greek name.

ܪܘܦܘܣ.note: The Greek writing of the Latin Rufus, red.

ܦܘܢܝܩܐ.note: The Greek name of the coast. The Syriac writes that name.

ܛܒܪܝܘܣ.note: The city named for the emperor Tiberius. The Greek writes it this way.

ܓܕܪܝܐ.note: A person of Gadara, the city east of the sea.

ܙܕܘܩܝܐ.note: The party takes its name from Zadok. The Greek writes Σαδδουκαῖος.

ܫܡܪܝܐ.note: A person of Samaria. The Greek writes Σαμαρίτης.

ܓܠܝܠܝܐ.note: The district. A Galilean is a person of it. The Greek writes Γαλιλαῖος.

ܐܪܡܝܐ.note: An Aramean. Where the Greek New Testament writes Ἕλλην, a Greek, this Peshitta often writes ܐܪܡܝܐ.

ܝܘܢܝܐ.note: Junia, greeted in Romans 16:7. The same Syriac letters also name the Greeks.

ܒܢܝܡܝܢ.note: Son of the right hand. The Greek writes Βενιαμίν.

ܫܠܬܐܝܠ.note: I asked of God. The Greek writes Σαλαθιήλ.

ܬܘ.note: The last letter. The Greek pair is Alpha and Omega.

ܐܠܦ.note: The first letter. The Greek pair is Alpha and Omega.
